t: This is Henry Wood Hall in Trinity Church Square, Southwark. It was built as Holy Trinity Church, designed in 1823 and 1824 by Francis Octavius Bedford, who designed four Greek Revival churches in south London in the 1820s. The church is now redundant, and the building is used as an orchestral rehearsal and recording studio. It's named after Sir Henry Wood, the conductor best known for the Proms, which he conducted for nearly fifty years. After his death the concerts were officially renamed the Henry Wood Promenade Concerts in his honour.
